classes.name: manifest
classes.reason: Each round's manifest read (_read_staged(manifest(workdir, r, placing), ...)) is sandwiched between two barrier.wait() calls, so every other rank is held at the second barrier until the reading rank finishes, coupling all ranks to that single access; since the path embeds the round index r, each distinct manifest file is opened and read exactly once per rank, and no time budget is enforced on it.

classes.name: sidecar
classes.reason: The sidecar reads (`for i in range(sidecars_per_rank(cell)): _read(sidecar(workdir, me, i, placing), SIDECAR_BYTES)`) occur after the round's barrier pair with no further synchronization point, so while one rank reads its sidecars the others are doing their own independent sidecar/shard work rather than waiting, meaning only the accessing rank blocks; because the index i does not depend on the round r, the same sidecar file is reopened and read once per round for all cell.rounds=200 rounds.

classes.name: shard
classes.reason: The shard reads (`for i in range(cell.shards_per_rank): _read(shard(workdir, me, i), SHARD_BYTES)`) run in the same unguarded segment as the sidecar reads, with no barrier forcing other ranks to wait on this specific access, so only the reading rank is blocked; since shard(workdir, rank, i) doesn't vary with round index, the same shard file is re-read every one of the cell.rounds=200 iterations, and there is no deadline logic around it.
